---
title: "Formulaic pattern-breaking in the Iliad"
date: 2025-12-14
description: >
  Does Homer break formulaic patterns at emotionally significant moments? An
  information-theoretic analysis of the Iliad measures how surprising each formula is
  given its context, and asks whether high-surprisal deviations cluster at narrative
  climaxes such as deaths and armour exchanges. Work in progress.
categories: [Digital humanities, Psycholinguistics]
greek: true          # this entry gets the Greek-letter scramble on its title
repo: https://github.com/ellacapellini/homeric-formula-deviation
---

**Idea.** When an audience expects one formula and hears another, the prediction error
makes that moment stand out. The project tests whether Homer uses this on purpose,
in the way Dante's *-ice* rhyme quietly evokes Beatrice in Inferno V.

**Method.** Surprisal is $-\log_2 P(\text{formula} \mid \text{context})$. Formulae are
extracted from the Perseus text of the *Iliad*, collected into a vocabulary, and
scored for deviation; the results can be explored in an interactive plot.

**Preliminary results.** Across 581 character mentions in 15,683 lines, about 23% show
a deviation. High-surprisal cases include the formula at Hector's death and the armour
formula when Patroclus wears Achilles' armour. These are early findings; the
correlation with narrative structure still has to be established.
